summary.short: Amends the Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act. Employers relying solely on AI analysis of video interviews must report applicants' race and ethnicity data annually to the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity; the Department reports yearly on whether the data shows racial bias.
summary.long: House Bill 53 adds Section 20 to the Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act (820 ILCS 42/20). Under subsection (a), an employer that relies solely upon an artificial intelligence analysis of a video interview to determine whether an applicant will be selected for an in-person interview must collect and report the race and ethnicity of applicants who are and are not afforded an in-person interview after the AI analysis, and the race and ethnicity of applicants who are hired. Under subsection (b), this data must be reported to the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity annually by December 31, covering the 12-month period ending on November 30 preceding the filing. Under subsection (c), the Department must analyze the reported data and report to the Governor and General Assembly by July 1 of each year whether the data discloses a racial bias in the use of artificial intelligence. The text sets no numeric thresholds, penalties or effective date.

Its numbers are procedural: the annual reporting deadline (December 31), the 12-month data period ending November 30, and the July 1 report date, which are coded as events, not thresholds.
